decisions.reason: As a core-adjacent camera with its own product page in both 2023 and 2024, it reflects visible commitment and sunk development effort, so management is likely to keep it despite no highlighted market win yet.
This modular camera line has strong public commitment, several models, and a visible ESA HERA mission success, which makes withdrawal very unlikely.
The sensor suite builds on established capabilities and remained prominently presented in both years, so management can justify persistence by treating any weak traction as temporary.

Although only mentioned rather than fully featured, the miniaturized space-qualified LiDAR fits the firm's announced push toward compact advanced sensors, so sunk R&D and strategic fit still favor retention.
As a newly launched radiation-hard camera line with several models and its own page, it already embodies a meaningful public and technical commitment that management is unlikely to reverse quickly.

Even with limited website prominence, the asteroid navigation and imaging camera is close to the firm's heritage and can be supported by recent deep-space mission visibility, so management is more likely to continue than to exit.
